Yes, I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin. (38:18).
Many are my enemies without cause, and many hate me without reason. (38:19).
Those who repay my good with evil attack me for pursuing the good. (38:20).
Do not forsake me, O LORD; be not far from me, O my God. (38:21).
Come quickly to help me, O Lord my Savior. (38:22).
crossRefs: Isaiah 53:4–5: Suffering imagery, borne iniquities.
Psalm 32:3–4: Silence and groaning under guilt.
Job 19:13–19: Friends and family withdraw in suffering.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָדְךָ נִכְבְּדָה (yadkha nikbedah), Greek: βαρεῖα χείρ σου, Aramaic: ידך תקיפא

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm laments deep physical, social, and spiritual anguish, pleading for God’s presence and help.

headings.text: Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger

stories.title: 🕰️ Psalms 39
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. I said, “I will watch my ways so that I will not sin with my tongue; I will guard my mouth with a muzzle as long as the wicked are present.” (39:1).
I was speechless and still; I remained silent, even from speaking good, and my sorrow was stirred. (39:2).
My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue: (39:3).
“Show me, O LORD, my end and the measure of my days. Let me know how fleeting my life is. (39:4).
You, indeed, have made my days as handbreadths, and my lifetime as nothing before You. Truly each man at his best exists as but a breath. Selah (39:5).
Surely every man goes about like a phantom; surely he bustles in vain; he heaps up riches not knowing who will haul them away. (39:6).
And now, O Lord, for what do I wait? My hope is in You. (39:7).
Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the reproach of fools. (39:8).
I have become mute; I do not open my mouth because of what You have done. (39:9).
Remove Your scourge from me; I am perishing by the force of Your hand. (39:10).
You discipline and correct a man for his iniquity, consuming like a moth what he holds dear; surely each man is but a vapor. Selah (39:11).
Hear my prayer, O LORD, and give ear to my cry for help; do not be deaf to my weeping. For I am a foreigner dwelling with You, a stranger like all my fathers. (39:12).
Turn Your gaze away from me, that I may again be cheered before I depart and am no more.” (39:13).
crossRefs: Psalm 90:10–12: Teach us to number our days.
James 4:14: Life is a mist that appears briefly.
Job 14:1–2: Human life like a flower and shadow.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הֶבֶל (hevel), Greek: ματαιότης, Aramaic: הבל

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm reflects on life’s shortness and asks God for mercy before death.

stories.title: 🎶 Psalms 40
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry. (40:1).
He lifted me up from the pit of despair, out of the miry clay; He set my feet upon a rock, and made my footsteps firm. (40:2).
He put a new song in my mouth, a hymn of praise to our God. Many will see and fear and put their trust in the LORD. (40:3).
Blessed is the man who has made the LORD his trust, who has not turned to the proud, nor to those who lapse into falsehood. (40:4).
Many, O LORD my God, are the wonders You have done, and the plans You have for us — none can compare to You — if I proclaim and declare them, they are more than I can count. (40:5).
Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but my ears You have opened. Burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not require. (40:6).
Then I said, “Here I am, I have come — it is written about me in the scroll: (40:7).
I delight to do Your will, O my God; Your law is within my heart.” (40:8).
I proclaim righteousness in the great assembly; behold, I do not seal my lips, as You, O LORD, do know. (40:9).
I have not covered up Your righteousness in my heart; I have declared Your faithfulness and salvation; I have not concealed Your loving devotion and faithfulness from the great assembly. (40:10).
O LORD, do not withhold Your mercy from me; Your loving devotion and faithfulness will always guard me. (40:11).
For evils without number surround me; my sins have overtaken me, so that I cannot see. They are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed within me. (40:12).
Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me; hurry, O LORD, to help me. (40:13).
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated. (40:14).
May those who say to me, “Aha, aha!” be appalled at their own shame. (40:15).
May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “The LORD be magnified!” (40:16).
But I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my helper and deliverer; O my God, do not delay. (40:17).
crossRefs: Hebrews 10:5–7: Quotes vv. 6–8 regarding sacrifice and obedience.
Psalm 27:6: Sacrifice of praise in God’s house.
1 Samuel 15:22: Obedience better than sacrifice.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בּוֹר (bor), Greek: λάκκος, Aramaic: בורא
translationNotes.note: A cistern-like pit, symbol of danger or death (v. 2).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי (aznayim karita li, 'dug ears for me'), Greek: σῶμα δὲ κατηρτίσω μοι ('a body prepared for me'), Aramaic: אודני פתח לי
translationNotes.note: Metaphor for readiness to obey; textual variation noted (v. 6).

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm thanks the LORD for rescue, declares obedience better than sacrifice, and prays for further deliverance.

headings.text: I Waited Patiently for the Lord

stories.title: 🤝 Psalms 41
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Blessed is the one who cares for the poor; the LORD will deliver him in the day of trouble. (41:1).
The LORD will protect and preserve him; He will bless him in the land and refuse to give him over to the will of his foes. (41:2).
The LORD will sustain him on his bed of illness and restore him from his bed of sickness. (41:3).
I said, “O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against You.” (41:4).
My enemies say with malice: “When will he die and be forgotten?” (41:5).
My visitor speaks falsehood; he gathers slander in his heart; he goes out and spreads it abroad. (41:6).
All who hate me whisper against me; they imagine the worst for me: (41:7).
“A vile disease has been poured into him; he will never get up from where he lies!” (41:8).
Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me. (41:9).
But You, O LORD, be gracious to me and raise me up, that I may repay them. (41:10).
By this I know that You delight in me, for my enemy does not triumph over me. (41:11).
In my integrity You uphold me and set me in Your presence forever. (41:12).
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen and Amen. (41:13).
crossRefs: John 13:18: “He who eats my bread has lifted his heel against me,” citing Psalm 41:9.
Proverbs 19:17: Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the LORD.
Psalm 37:17-24: The LORD upholds the righteous.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַשְׂכִּיל אֶל־דַּל (maskil el-dal); Greek (LXX): συνετός ἐστιν ἐπὶ πτωχόν
translationNotes.note: To act wisely toward the weak or poor (v. 1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הִגְדִּיל עָקֵב (higdil aqev); Greek: ἐπῆρεν ἐπ᾽ ἐμὲ πτέρναν

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm blesses care for the poor, laments betrayal by a close friend, and affirms the LORD’s sustaining presence.

stories.title: 💧 Psalms 42
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah. As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul longs after You, O God. (42:1).
My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When shall I come and appear in God’s presence? (42:2).
My tears have been my food both day and night, while men ask me all day long, “Where is your God?” (42:3).
These things come to mind as I pour out my soul: how I walked with the multitude, leading the festive procession to the house of God with shouts of joy and praise. (42:4).
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him for the salvation of His presence. (42:5).
O my God, my soul despairs within me. Therefore I remember You from the land of Jordan and the peaks of Hermon — even from Mount Mizar. (42:6).
Deep calls to deep in the roar of Your waterfalls; all Your breakers and waves have rolled over me. (42:7).
The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life. (42:8).
I say to God my Rock, “Why have You forgotten me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?” (42:9).
Like the crushing of my bones, my enemies taunt me, while they say to me all day long, “Where is your God?” (42:10).
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God. (42:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 63:1: Thirsting for God.
Jonah 2:3: “All Your waves and breakers passed over me.”
Psalm 43: Companion prayer with repeated refrain.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תִּשְׁתּוֹחֲחִי (tishetokhachi); Greek: καταπεφρόνηται ἡ ψυχή μου
Hebrew: תְּהוֹם אֶל־תְּהוֹם קוֹרֵא (tehom el-tehom qore); Greek: ἄβυσσος ἄβυσσον ἐπικαλεῖται
translationNotes.note: Poetic for surging waters; overwhelming distress (v. 7).

stories.keyTakeaway: Separated and taunted, the psalmist thirsts for God and repeatedly urges his soul to hope in Him.

headings.text: BOOK II As the Deer Pants for the Water

stories.title: 🕯️ Psalms 43
summaryBullets: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from deceitful and unjust men. (43:1).
For You are the God of my refuge. Why have You rejected me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression? (43:2).
Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to Your holy mountain and to the place where You dwell. (43:3).
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God. (43:4).
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God. (43:5).
crossRefs: Psalm 42:5-11: Identical refrain.
Psalm 27:1: The LORD is my light and salvation.
Psalm 43:3: Holy hill motif linked to Zion (cf. Psalm 2:6).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁפְטֵנִי (shafteni, ‘judge me’); Greek: κρῖνόν με
Hebrew: אוֹרְךָ וַאֲמִתֶּךָ (orkha va’amittekha); Greek: τὸ φῶς σου καὶ ἡ ἀλήθειά σου

stories.keyTakeaway: Seeking justice and guidance, the psalmist asks for God’s light and truth to bring him to worship.

stories.title: 🛡️ Psalms 44
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of the sons of Korah. We have heard with our ears, O God; our fathers have told us the work You did in their days, in the days of old. (44:1).
With Your hand You drove out the nations and planted our fathers there; You crushed the peoples and cast them out. (44:2).
For it was not by their sword that they took the land; their arm did not bring them victory. It was by Your right hand, Your arm, and the light of Your face, because You favored them. (44:3).
You are my King, O God, who ordains victories for Jacob. (44:4).
Through You we repel our foes; through Your name we trample our enemies. (44:5).
For I do not trust in my bow, nor does my sword save me. (44:6).
For You save us from our enemies; You put those who hate us to shame. (44:7).
In God we have boasted all day long, and Your name we will praise forever. Selah (44:8).
But You have rejected and humbled us; You no longer go forth with our armies. (44:9).
You have made us retreat from the foe, and those who hate us have plundered us. (44:10).
You have given us up as sheep to be devoured; You have scattered us among the nations. (44:11).
You sell Your people for nothing; no profit do You gain from their sale. (44:12).
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and derision to those around us. (44:13).
You have made us a byword among the nations, a laughingstock among the peoples. (44:14).
All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame has covered my face, (44:15).
at the voice of the scorner and reviler, because of the enemy, bent on revenge. (44:16).
All this has come upon us, though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant. (44:17).
Our hearts have not turned back; our steps have not strayed from Your path. (44:18).
But You have crushed us in the lair of jackals; You have covered us with deepest darkness. (44:19).
If we had forgotten the name of our God or spread out our hands to a foreign god, (44:20).
would not God have discovered, since He knows the secrets of the heart? (44:21).
Yet for Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered. (44:22).
Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise! Do not reject us forever. (44:23).
Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and oppression? (44:24).
For our soul has sunk to the dust; our bodies cling to the earth. (44:25).
Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion. (44:26).
crossRefs: Romans 8:36: “We are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered,” citing Psalm 44:22.
Joshua 24:12: Victory not by Israel’s sword.
Psalm 60: Another communal lament seeking help.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צֹאן טִבְחָה (tson tivchah); Greek: πρόβατα σφαγῆς
Hebrew: פָּדָה (padah), Greek: λύτρωσαι, Aramaic: פרק

stories.keyTakeaway: The community laments defeat despite professed loyalty and pleads for God to rise and redeem.

stories.title: 💍 Psalms 45
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lilies.” A Maskil of the sons of Korah. A love song. My heart is stirred by a noble theme as I recite my verses to the king; my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer. (45:1).
You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. (45:2).
Strap your sword at your side, O mighty warrior; appear in your majesty and splendor. (45:3).
In your splendor ride forth in victory on behalf of truth and humility and justice; may your right hand show your awesome deeds. (45:4).
Your arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s foes; the nations fall beneath your feet. (45:5).
Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom. (45:6).
You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you above your companions with the oil of joy. (45:7).
All your garments are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia; from palaces of ivory the harps make you glad. (45:8).
The daughters of kings are among your honored women; the queen stands at your right hand, adorned with the gold of Ophir. (45:9).
Listen, O daughter! Consider and incline your ear: Forget your people and your father’s house, (45:10).
and the king will desire your beauty; bow to him, for he is your lord. (45:11).
The Daughter of Tyre will come with a gift; men of wealth will seek your favor. (45:12).
All glorious is the princess in her chamber; her gown is embroidered with gold. (45:13).
In colorful garments she is led to the king; her virgin companions are brought before you. (45:14).
They are led in with joy and gladness; they enter the palace of the king. (45:15).
Your sons will succeed your fathers; you will make them princes throughout the land. (45:16).
I will commemorate your name through all generations; therefore the nations will praise you forever and ever. (45:17).
crossRefs: Hebrews 1:8–9: Cites Psalm 45:6–7 about the throne and anointing.
Song of Songs 3:6–11: Royal wedding imagery.
1 Kings 1:39: Anointing associated with kingship.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֵׁבֶט מִישׁוֹר (shevet mishor); Greek: ῥάβδος εὐθύτητος
Hebrew: מְשַׁחֲךָ אֱלֹהִים שֶׁמֶן שָׂשׂוֹן (meshachakha… shemen sason); Greek: ἔχρισέν σε… ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως

translationNotes.note: A fragrant gum resin from the Commiphora tree of Arabia and East Africa. Used as a holy anointing-oil ingredient (Exodus 30:23), as perfume, as an embalming spice (John 19:39), and, mixed with wine, as a pain-dulling drink (Mark 15:23). One of the magi's gifts.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֹר (mor); Greek: σμύρνα (smurna)

stories.keyTakeaway: A wedding ode praises the king’s beauty, rule, and anointing, and describes the bride’s entrance and future offspring.

headings.text: My Heart Is Stirred by a Noble Theme

stories.title: 🏔️ Psalms 46
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. A song. God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in times of trouble. (46:1).
Therefore we will not fear, though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas, (46:2).
though their waters roar and foam and the mountains quake in the surge. Selah (46:3).
There is a river whose streams delight the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells. (46:4).
God is within her; she will not be moved. God will help her when morning dawns. (46:5).
Nations rage, kingdoms crumble; the earth melts when He lifts His voice. (46:6).
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah (46:7).
Come, see the works of the LORD, who brings devastation upon the earth. (46:8).
He makes wars to cease throughout the earth; He breaks the bow and shatters the spear; He burns the shields in the fire. (46:9).
“Be still and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted over the earth.” (46:10).
The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress. Selah (46:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 48:1–8: City of God imagery.
Isaiah 2:4: Weapons broken; nations cease from war.
Habakkuk 2:20: Silent awe before God.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַחֲסֶה (machaseh), Greek: καταφυγή, Aramaic: מחסיא
Hebrew: הַרְפּוּ (harpu); Greek: σχολάσατε

stories.keyTakeaway: Amid upheaval and war, the psalm declares God present as refuge, commanding stillness and announcing His exaltation.

headings.text: God Is Our Refuge and Strength

stories.title: 👏 Psalms 47
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you peoples; shout unto God with a voice of triumph. (47:1).
How awesome is the LORD Most High, the great King over all the earth! (47:2).
He subdues nations beneath us, and peoples under our feet. (47:3).
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom He loves. Selah (47:4).
God has ascended amid shouts of joy, the LORD with the sound of the horn. (47:5).
Sing praises to God, sing praises; sing praises to our King, sing praises! (47:6).
For God is King of all the earth; sing to Him a psalm of praise. (47:7).
God reigns over the nations; God is seated on His holy throne. (47:8).
The nobles of the nations have assembled as the people of the God of Abraham; for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is highly exalted. (47:9).
crossRefs: Psalm 93:1: The LORD reigns; He is robed in majesty.
Psalm 2:8: Nations as inheritance.
1 Chronicles 16:31: Let the nations say, “The LORD reigns.”

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֶלְיוֹן (ʿElyon), Greek: ὕψιστος, Aramaic: עילאה

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm summons global praise because the LORD reigns as King over all nations.

headings.text: Clap Your Hands, All You Peoples

stories.title: 🏙️ Psalms 48
summaryBullets: A song. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain. (48:1).
Beautiful in loftiness, the joy of all the earth, like the peaks of Zaphon is Mount Zion, the city of the great King. (48:2).
God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress. (48:3).
For behold, the kings assembled; they all advanced together. (48:4).
They saw and were astounded; they fled in terror. (48:5).
Trembling seized them there, anguish like a woman in labor. (48:6).
With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish. (48:7).
As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts, in the city of our God: God will establish her forever. Selah (48:8).
Within Your temple, O God, we contemplate Your loving devotion. (48:9).
Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness. (48:10).
Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments. (48:11).
March around Zion, encircle her, count her towers, (48:12).
consider her ramparts, tour her citadels, that you may tell the next generation. (48:13).
For this God is our God forever and ever; He will be our guide even till death. (48:14).
crossRefs: Psalm 46: God’s city unshaken.
Isaiah 33:20–22: Zion as secure habitation with the LORD as King.
Psalm 122:3–5: Jerusalem built as a city bound firmly together.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֵיל / אַרְמְנוֹת (cheil / armonot); Greek: τεῖχος / παλάτια

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm celebrates Zion’s security under the LORD and calls eyewitness remembrance for future generations.

stories.title: 💬 Psalms 49
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples; listen, all inhabitants of the world, (49:1).
both low and high, rich and poor alike. (49:2).
My mouth will impart wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding. (49:3).
I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will express my riddle with the harp: (49:4).
Why should I fear in times of trouble, when wicked usurpers surround me? (49:5).
They trust in their wealth and boast in their great riches. (49:6).
No man can possibly redeem his brother or pay his ransom to God. (49:7).
For the redemption of his soul is costly, and never can payment suffice, (49:8).
that he should live on forever and not see decay. (49:9).
For it is clear that wise men die, and the foolish and the senseless both perish and leave their wealth to others. (49:10).
Their graves are their eternal homes — their dwellings for endless generations — even though their lands were their namesakes. (49:11).
But a man, despite his wealth, cannot endure; he is like the beasts that perish. (49:12).
This is the fate of the foolish and their followers who endorse their sayings. Selah (49:13).
Like sheep they are destined for Sheol. Death will be their shepherd. The upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol, far from their lofty abode. (49:14).
But God will redeem my life from Sheol, for He will surely take me to Himself. Selah (49:15).
Do not be afraid when a man grows rich, when the splendor of his house increases. (49:16).
For when he dies, he will carry nothing away; his abundance will not follow him down. (49:17).
Though in his lifetime he blesses his soul — and men praise you when you prosper — (49:18).
he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day. (49:19).
A man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish. (49:20).
crossRefs: Luke 12:15–21: Parable of the rich fool.
Ecclesiastes 5:13–15: Wealth left at death.
Matthew 16:26: What will a man give in exchange for his soul?

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פָּדָה (padah) / כֹּפֶר (kofer, ransom price); Greek: λυτρόομαι / λύτρον

translationNotes.note: The Old Testament realm of the dead; a shadowy underworld where both righteous and wicked descend (Genesis 37:35; Psalm 16:10). Not necessarily a place of torment; more a state of cessation and silence. The Septuagint and New Testament render it with the Greek word hades.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (sheol)

stories.keyTakeaway: Wealth cannot redeem from death; the psalm warns against trusting riches and states God ransoms from Sheol.

stories.title: 🔥 Psalms 50
summaryBullets: A Psalm of Asaph. The Mighty One, God the LORD, speaks and summons the earth from where the sun rises to where it sets. (50:1).
From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth. (50:2).
Our God approaches and will not be silent! Consuming fire precedes Him, and a tempest rages around Him. (50:3).
He summons the heavens above, and the earth, that He may judge His people: (50:4).
“Gather to Me My saints, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.” (50:5).
And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is Judge. Selah (50:6).
“Hear, O My people, and I will speak, O Israel, and I will testify against you: I am God, your God. (50:7).
I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices, and your burnt offerings are ever before Me. (50:8).
I have no need for a bull from your stall or goats from your pens, (50:9).
for every beast of the forest is Mine — the cattle on a thousand hills. (50:10).
I know every bird in the mountains, and the creatures of the field are Mine. (50:11).
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and the fullness thereof. (50:12).
Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? (50:13).
Sacrifice a thank offering to God, and fulfill your vows to the Most High. (50:14).
Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me.” (50:15).
To the wicked, however, God says, “What right have you to recite My statutes and to bear My covenant on your lips? (50:16).
For you hate My instruction and cast My words behind you. (50:17).
When you see a thief, you befriend him, and throw in your lot with adulterers. (50:18).
You unleash your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit. (50:19).
You sit and malign your brother; you slander your own mother’s son. (50:20).
You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought I was just like you. But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face. (50:21).
Now consider this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you: (50:22).
He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God.” (50:23).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 15:22: Obedience better than sacrifice.
Isaiah 1:11–17: Rebuke of sacrifices without justice.
Hebrews 13:15: Sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips.

translationNotes.term: The Mighty One, God the LORD
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵל אֱלֹהִים יְהוָה (El Elohim YHWH); Greek: ὁ Θεὸς θεῶν κύριος
Hebrew: זֶבַח תּוֹדָה (zevach todah); Greek: θυσία αἰνέσεως

stories.keyTakeaway: God appears as judge from Zion, commands true thanksgiving and obedience rather than trust in sacrificial quantity.

stories.title: 🫧 Psalms 51
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. When Nathan the prophet came to him after his adultery with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your loving devotion; according to Your great compassion, blot out my transgressions. (51:1).
Wash me clean of my iniquity and cleanse me from my sin. (51:2).
For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me. (51:3).
Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be proved right when You speak and blameless when You judge. (51:4).
Surely I was brought forth in iniquity; I was sinful when my mother conceived me. (51:5).
Surely You desire truth in the inmost being; You teach me wisdom in the inmost place. (51:6).
Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow. (51:7).
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones You have crushed rejoice. (51:8).
Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities. (51:9).
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. (51:10).
Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me. (51:11).
Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit. (51:12).
Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You. (51:13).
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness. (51:14).
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise. (51:15).
For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings. (51:16).
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise. (51:17).
In Your good pleasure, cause Zion to prosper; build up the walls of Jerusalem. (51:18).
Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in whole burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on Your altar. (51:19).
crossRefs: 2 Samuel 12:13: David confesses after Nathan confronts him.
Exodus 12:22: Hyssop used in ritual application of blood.
Psalm 32:1–5: Confession and forgiveness described.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּרָא (bara), Greek (LXX): κτίζω (ktizō), Aramaic: ברא (bara)
translationNotes.note: Bring into being; request for a clean heart (v. 10).

A small, fragrant herb (Origanum syriacum / Syrian oregano), growing in rocky soil. Bunches of hyssop were used to apply Passover blood to the doorposts (Exodus 12:22), in leper-cleansing rituals (Leviticus 14:6), and held up to Jesus on the cross with a wine-soaked sponge (John 19:29).
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵזוֹב (ezov); Greek: ὕσσωπος (hussopos)

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm is a confession asking for cleansing, a new heart, and restored joy, ending with sacrifices offered after contrition.

headings.text: Create in Me a Clean Heart, O God

stories.title: 🌿 Psalms 52
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Maskil of David. After Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.” Why do you boast of evil, O mighty man? The loving devotion of God endures all day long. (52:1).
Your tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, O worker of deceit. (52:2).
You love evil more than good, falsehood more than speaking truth. Selah (52:3).
You love every word that devours, O deceitful tongue. (52:4).
Surely God will bring you down to everlasting ruin; He will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent; He will uproot you from the land of the living. Selah (52:5).
The righteous will see and fear; they will mock the evildoer, saying, (52:6).
“Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.” (52:7).
But I am like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God; I trust in the loving devotion of God forever and ever. (52:8).
I will praise You forever, because You have done it. I will wait on Your name — for it is good — in the presence of Your saints. (52:9).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 22:9–19: Doeg the Edomite reports and bloodshed follows (historical backdrop of the heading).
James 3:5–8: The tongue’s destructive power.
Jeremiah 11:16: Israel likened to a green olive tree.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גִּבּוֹר (gibbor), Greek (LXX): δυνατός, Aramaic: גבורא
Hebrew: תַּעַר מֻלָּט (taʿar mullat); Greek: ξυρὸν ἀκονητόν

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm denounces a destructive tongue and contrasts it with trust like a green olive tree in God’s house.

headings.text: Why Do You Boast of Evil?

stories.title: 🚫 Psalms 53
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David. The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good. (53:1).
God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God. (53:2).
All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one. (53:3).
Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God. (53:4).
There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them. (53:5).
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad! (53:6).
crossRefs: Romans 3:10–12: Citation of “none righteous… none who does good.”
Psalm 14: Close parallel of this psalm’s wording.
Isaiah 59:7–8: Portrait of pervasive injustice.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נָבָל (naval), Greek (LXX): ἄφρων, Aramaic: נבל
Hebrew: שׁוּב שְׁבוּת (shuv shevut); Greek: ἐπιστρέψει αἰχμαλωσίαν

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm states universal corruption and ends with a call for salvation from Zion.

headings.text: The Fool Says There Is No God

stories.title: 🛡️ Psalms 54
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. When the Ziphites went to Saul and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might! (54:1).
Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth. (54:2).
For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life — men with no regard for God. Selah (54:3).
Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul. (54:4).
He will reward my enemies with evil. In Your faithfulness, destroy them. (54:5).
Freely I will sacrifice to You; I will praise Your name, O LORD, for it is good. (54:6).
For He has delivered me from every trouble, and my eyes have looked in triumph on my foes. (54:7).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 23:19; 26:1: Ziphites report David (heading background).
Proverbs 18:10: The name of the LORD is a strong tower.
Psalm 116:17: Sacrifice of thanksgiving called a freewill offering.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֵׁם (shem), Greek: ὄνομα, Aramaic: שׁום
Hebrew: נְדָבָה (nedavah), Greek: προαίρεσις (sense), Aramaic: נדבתא

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm petitions for rescue by God’s name, affirms God as helper, and vows freewill sacrifice and thanks.

stories.title: 🕊️ Psalms 55
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David. Listen to my prayer, O God, and do not ignore my plea. (55:1).
Attend to me and answer me. I am restless in my complaint, and distraught (55:2).
at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked. For they bring down disaster upon me and resent me in their anger. (55:3).
My heart pounds within me, and the terrors of death assail me. (55:4).
Fear and trembling grip me, and horror has overwhelmed me. (55:5).
I said, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest. (55:6).
How far away I would flee! In the wilderness I would remain. Selah (55:7).
I would hurry to my shelter, far from this raging tempest.” (55:8).
O Lord, confuse and confound their speech, for I see violence and strife in the city. (55:9).
Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within. (55:10).
Destruction is within; oppression and deceit never leave the streets. (55:11).
For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide. (55:12).
But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend. (55:13).
We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God. (55:14).
Let death seize them by surprise; let them go down to Sheol alive, for evil is with them in their homes. (55:15).
But I call to God, and the LORD saves me. (55:16).
Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice. (55:17).
He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me. (55:18).
God will hear and humiliate them — the One enthroned for the ages — Selah because they do not change and they have no fear of God. (55:19).
My companion attacks his friends; he violates his covenant. (55:20).
His speech is smooth as butter, but war is in his heart. His words are softer than oil, yet they are swords unsheathed. (55:21).
Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken. (55:22).
But You, O God, will bring them down to the Pit of destruction; men of bloodshed and deceit will not live out half their days. But I will trust in You. (55:23).
crossRefs: 2 Samuel 15–17: David’s betrayal context (Absalom/Ahithophel) echoes the theme.
John 13:18: Betrayal by one who ate bread with him (parallel idea).
1 Peter 5:7: Cast all anxieties on Him.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יְהָבְךָ (yehavkha), Greek (LXX): μέριμνά σου, Aramaic: יהבך
translationNotes.note: Load/what is given; cast upon the LORD (v. 22).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי / אַלּוּף (ish shelomi / alluf); Greek: ὁ ἑταῖρός μου

translationNotes.note: The Old Testament realm of the dead; a shadowy underworld where both righteous and wicked descend (Genesis 37:35; Psalm 16:10). Not necessarily a place of torment; more a state of cessation and silence. The Septuagint and New Testament render it with the Greek word hades.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (sheol)

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm laments treachery by a companion, describes city violence, and urges casting one’s burden on the LORD.

headings.text: Cast Your Burden upon the Lord

stories.title: 🧪 Psalms 56
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack. (56:1).
My enemies pursue me all day long, for many proudly assail me. (56:2).
When I am afraid, I put my trust in You. (56:3).
In God, whose word I praise — in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? (56:4).
All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are on my demise. (56:5).
They conspire, they lurk, they watch my steps while they wait to take my life. (56:6).
In spite of such sin, will they escape? In Your anger, O God, cast down the nations. (56:7).
You have taken account of my wanderings. Put my tears in Your bottle — are they not in Your book? (56:8).
Then my enemies will retreat on the day I cry for help. By this I will know that God is on my side. (56:9).
In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise, (56:10).
in God I trust; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me? (56:11).
Your vows are upon me, O God; I will render thank offerings to You. (56:12).
For You have delivered my soul from death, and my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of life. (56:13).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 21:10–15: David seized in Gath (heading background).
Psalm 118:6: “What can man do to me?”
Revelation 5:8: Bowls of incense as prayers (collecting imagery).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּשָׂר (basar), Greek: σάρξ, Aramaic: בשרא
Hebrew: נֹאד (noʾd), Greek: ἀσκός, Aramaic: נאדא
translationNotes.note: Skin bottle for liquids; image for preserving tears (v. 8).

stories.keyTakeaway: Amid constant attack, the psalmist declares trust in God, mentions tears kept in a bottle, and vows thanks after deliverance.

headings.text: Be Merciful to Me, O God

stories.title: 🪽 Psalms 57
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy, for in You my soul takes refuge. In the shadow of Your wings I will take shelter until the danger has passed. (57:1).
I cry out to God Most High, to God who fulfills His purpose for me. (57:2).
He reaches down from heaven and saves me; He rebukes those who trample me. Selah God sends forth His loving devotion and His truth. (57:3).
My soul is among the lions; I lie down with ravenous beasts— with men whose teeth are spears and arrows, whose tongues are sharp swords. (57:4).
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth. (57:5).
They spread a net for my feet; my soul was despondent. They dug a pit before me, but they themselves have fallen into it! Selah (57:6).
My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast. I will sing and make music. (57:7).
Awake, my glory! Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn. (57:8).
I will praise You, O Lord, among the nations; I will sing Your praises among the peoples. (57:9).
For Your loving devotion reaches to the heavens, and Your faithfulness to the clouds. (57:10).
Be exalted, O God, above the heavens; may Your glory cover all the earth. (57:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 17:8: Hide me in the shadow of Your wings.
Psalm 108:1–5: Shared lines of praise and steadfast heart.
Ruth 2:12: Seeking refuge under God’s wings (motif).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ (betzel kenafekha), Greek: ἐν σκέπῃ τῶν πτερύγων σου, Aramaic: בְּטִל צִפְּרַפָּךְ
Hebrew: נָכוֹן (nakhon), Greek: ἑτοίμη, Aramaic: מתקן

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm seeks refuge under God’s wings, describes traps set by men, and calls for God’s exaltation and worldwide praise.

headings.text: In You My Soul Takes Refuge

stories.title: 🦷 Psalms 58
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David. Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men? (58:1).
No, in your hearts you devise injustice; with your hands you mete out violence on the earth. (58:2).
The wicked are estranged from the womb; the liars go astray from birth. (58:3).
Their venom is like the venom of a snake, like a cobra that shuts its ears, (58:4).
refusing to hear the tune of the charmer who skillfully weaves his spell. (58:5).
O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths; O LORD, tear out the fangs of the lions. (58:6).
May they vanish like water that runs off; when they draw the bow, may their arrows be blunted. (58:7).
Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun. (58:8).
Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away. (58:9).
The righteous will rejoice when they see they are avenged; they will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked. (58:10).
Then men will say, “There is surely a reward for the righteous! There is surely a God who judges the earth!” (58:11).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 16:18–20: Command to judge justly.
Isaiah 59:14–15: Justice turned back; truth stumbles.
Psalm 68:23: Feet bathed in the blood of enemies (violent victory image).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵלֶם/אֵלִם (ʾelem/ʾelim; textual issue), Greek (LXX): συνεκροτήσατε ἀληθῆ, Aramaic: דיינין
translationNotes.note: Uncertain reading; likely addresses human judges (v. 1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פֶּתֶן (pethen), Greek: ἀσπίς, Aramaic: פתנא

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm charges rulers with injustice and petitions graphic judgment, concluding that God judges on earth.

stories.title: 🐕 Psalms 59
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him. Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise against me. (59:1).
Deliver me from workers of iniquity, and save me from men of bloodshed. (59:2).
See how they lie in wait for me. Fierce men conspire against me for no transgression or sin of my own, O LORD. (59:3).
For no fault of my own, they move swiftly to attack me. Arise to help me, and take notice. (59:4).
O LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; show no mercy to the wicked traitors. Selah (59:5).
They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city. (59:6).
See what they spew from their mouths— sharp words from their lips: “For who can hear us?” (59:7).
But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You scoff at all the nations. (59:8).
I will keep watch for You, O my strength, because You, O God, are my fortress. (59:9).
My God of loving devotion will come to meet me; God will let me stare down my foes. (59:10).
Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Scatter them by Your power, and bring them down, O Lord, our shield. (59:11).
By the sins of their mouths and the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride, in the curses and lies they utter. (59:12).
Consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, so it may be known to the ends of the earth that God rules over Jacob. Selah (59:13).
They return in the evening, snarling like dogs and prowling around the city. (59:14).
They scavenge for food, and growl if they are not satisfied. (59:15).
But I will sing of Your strength and proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning. For You are my fortress, my refuge in times of trouble. (59:16).
To You, O my strength, I sing praises, for You, O God, are my fortress, my God of loving devotion. (59:17).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 19:11: Men watch David’s house to kill him (heading background).
Psalm 2:4: The LORD laughs at opponents.
Psalm 18:2: The LORD my fortress and deliverer.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַנְשֵׁי דָמִים (anshei damim), Greek: ἄνδρες αἱμάτων, Aramaic: גברי דמיא
Hebrew: מִשְׂגָּב (misgav), Greek: καταφυγή/ὑπερασπιστής, Aramaic: משגבָא

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm pleads for rescue from murderous watchers and contrasts their nightly prowling with morning praise for God the fortress.

stories.title: 🏴 Psalms 60
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us! (60:1).
You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking. (60:2).
You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink. (60:3).
You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah (60:4).
Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered. (60:5).
God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth. (60:6).
Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter. (60:7).
Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.” (60:8).
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom? (60:9).
Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies? (60:10).
Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless. (60:11).
With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies. (60:12).
crossRefs: Psalm 108:6–13: Parallel composition with similar oracle.
2 Samuel 8:1–14: Campaigns against surrounding nations (historical frame).
Numbers 34:1–12: Boundary descriptions for the land (geographic context).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עַל־אֱדוֹם אַשְׁלִיךְ נַעֲלִי (ʿal Edom ashlich naʿali); Greek: ἐπ᾽ Ἰδουμαίαν βαλῶ τὸ ὑπόδημά μου

translationNotes.term: Vain is the salvation of man
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁוְא תְּשׁוּעַת אָדָם (shav teshuaʿat adam); Greek: μάταιος ἡ σωτηρία ἀνθρώπου
translationNotes.note: Human deliverance is futile without God (v. 11).

stories.keyTakeaway: After describing national rejection and shaking, the psalm records God’s territorial claims and asks for help, declaring human deliverance vain and victory with God.

stories.title: 🪨 Psalms 61
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David. Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer. (61:1).
From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I. (61:2).
For You have been my refuge, a tower of strength against the enemy. (61:3).
Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings. Selah (61:4).
For You have heard my vows, O God; You have given me the inheritance reserved for those who fear Your name. (61:5).
Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations. (61:6).
May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever; appoint Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness to guard him. (61:7).
Then I will ever sing praise to Your name and fulfill my vows day by day. (61:8).
crossRefs: 2 Samuel 7:13–16: Promise of enduring kingship.
Proverbs 18:10: The name of the LORD is a strong tower.
Psalm 91:4: Refuge under His wings.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צוּר (tsur) / מִגְדַּל־עֹז (migdal-ʿoz), Greek: πέτρα / πύργος ἰσχυρός, Aramaic: טוּר / מגדלא דּעוּז
Hebrew: כָּנָף (kanaf), Greek: πτέρυγες, Aramaic: כנפין

translationNotes.note: The distance between thumb-tip and little-finger-tip with the fingers spread; half a cubit, about 9 inches (23 cm). The breastpiece of the high priest was a span square (Exodus 28:16).
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: זֶרֶת (zeret)

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm petitions God for refuge and for long life for the king, with vows of continual praise.

stories.title: 🕊️ Psalms 62
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. In God alone my soul finds rest; my salvation comes from Him. (62:1).
He alone is my rock and my salvation. He is my fortress; I will never be shaken. (62:2).
How long will you threaten a man? Will all of you throw him down like a leaning wall or a tottering fence? (62:3).
They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch; they delight in lies; with their mouths they bless, but inwardly they curse. Selah (62:4).
Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him. (62:5).
He alone is my rock and my salvation; He is my fortress; I will not be shaken. (62:6).
My salvation and my honor rest on God, my strong rock; my refuge is in God. (62:7).
Trust in Him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our refuge. Selah (62:8).
Lowborn men are but a vapor; the exalted are but a lie. Weighed on the scale, they go up; together they are but a vapor. (62:9).
Place no trust in extortion or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them. (62:10).
God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God, (62:11).
and loving devotion to You, O Lord. For You will repay each man according to his deeds. (62:12).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 9:23–24: Do not boast in wisdom, might, or riches.
Proverbs 11:28: He who trusts in riches will fall.
Romans 2:6: God will render to each one according to his works.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַךְ (ʾakh), Greek (LXX): πλὴν / μόνον, Aramaic: בַּר מִן
Hebrew: דּוּמִיָּה (dumiyyah), Greek: σιγή, Aramaic: שתוקא

stories.keyTakeaway: Exclusive trust is placed in God rather than in people, force, or wealth; God repays each according to his work.

stories.title: 🌵 Psalms 63
summaryBullets: A Psalm of David, when he was in the Wilderness of Judah. O God, You are my God. Earnestly I seek You; my soul thirsts for You. My body yearns for You in a dry and weary land without water. (63:1).
So I have seen You in the sanctuary and beheld Your power and glory. (63:2).
Because Your loving devotion is better than life, my lips will glorify You. (63:3).
So I will bless You as long as I live; in Your name I will lift my hands. (63:4).
My soul is satisfied as with the richest of foods; with joyful lips my mouth will praise You. (63:5).
When I remember You on my bed, I think of You through the watches of the night. (63:6).
For You are my help; I will sing for joy in the shadow of Your wings. (63:7).
My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me. (63:8).
But those who seek my life to destroy it will go into the depths of the earth. (63:9).
They will fall to the power of the sword; they will become a portion for foxes. (63:10).
But the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by Him will exult, for the mouths of liars will be shut. (63:11).
crossRefs: Psalm 42:1–2: Thirsting for God.
Deuteronomy 10:20: Cling to the LORD.
Psalm 36:8: Satisfaction with God’s abundance.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: דָּבַק (davaq), Greek: κολλάομαι, Aramaic: דבק
Hebrew: חֶסֶד (ḥesed), Greek: ἔλεος, Aramaic: חסדא

stories.keyTakeaway: In wilderness longing, the psalmist declares God’s love better than life, clings to God, and states the downfall of those seeking his life.

stories.title: 🏹 Psalms 64
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. Hear, O God, my voice of complaint; preserve my life from dread of the enemy. (64:1).
Hide me from the scheming of the wicked, from the mob of workers of iniquity, (64:2).
who sharpen their tongues like swords and aim their bitter words like arrows, (64:3).
ambushing the innocent in seclusion, shooting suddenly, without fear. (64:4).
They hold fast to their evil purpose; they speak of hiding their snares. “Who will see them?” they say. (64:5).
They devise injustice and say, “We have perfected a secret plan.” For the inner man and the heart are mysterious. (64:6).
But God will shoot them with arrows; suddenly they will be wounded. (64:7).
They will be made to stumble, their own tongues turned against them. All who see will shake their heads. (64:8).
Then all mankind will fear and proclaim the work of God; so they will ponder what He has done. (64:9).
Let the righteous rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in Him; let all the upright in heart exult. (64:10).
crossRefs: Psalm 7:15–16: Pitfall turned back on the wicked.
James 3:5–8: Tongue as a destructive weapon.
Proverbs 26:27: He who digs a pit will fall into it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לָשׁוֹן (lashon) / חִצִּים (ḥitsim), Greek: γλῶσσα / ἄρθρα/βελεμνά, Aramaic: לישן / חיצין

stories.keyTakeaway: Secret slander and ambush are reversed when God strikes and makes the wicked fall by their own words.

stories.title: 🌾 Psalms 65
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion; to You our vows will be fulfilled. (65:1).
O You who listen to prayer, all people will come to You. (65:2).
When iniquities prevail against me, You atone for our transgressions. (65:3).
Blessed is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts! We are filled with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your temple. (65:4).
With awesome deeds of righteousness You answer us, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of the farthest seas. (65:5).
You formed the mountains by Your power, having girded Yourself with might. (65:6).
You stilled the roaring of the seas, the pounding of their waves, and the tumult of the nations. (65:7).
Those who live far away fear Your wonders; You make the dawn and sunset shout for joy. (65:8).
You attend to the earth and water it; with abundance You enrich it. The streams of God are full of water, for You prepare our grain by providing for the earth. (65:9).
You soak its furrows and level its ridges; You soften it with showers and bless its growth. (65:10).
You crown the year with Your bounty, and Your paths overflow with plenty. (65:11).
The pastures of the wilderness overflow; the hills are robed with joy. (65:12).
The pastures are clothed with flocks, and the valleys are decked with grain. They shout in triumph; indeed, they sing. (65:13).
crossRefs: Leviticus 16:30: Atonement brings cleansing.
Psalm 104:13–15: God waters and makes things grow.
Isaiah 55:10–12: Rain, fruitfulness, and joy.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כִּפֶּר (kipper), Greek (LXX): ἐξιλάσκομαι, Aramaic: כפר
Hebrew: תַּעְטְרֶנָּה (taʿtrennah), Greek: ἐστεφάνωσας, Aramaic: כללת שתא
translationNotes.note: Figurative for loading the year with goodness (v. 11).

stories.keyTakeaway: God is praised as the atoning hearer of prayer, ruler of creation, and provider of an abundant harvest.

stories.title: 📣 Psalms 66
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A song. A Psalm. Make a joyful noise to God, all the earth! (66:1).
Sing the glory of His name; make His praise glorious. (66:2).
Say to God, “How awesome are Your deeds! So great is Your power that Your enemies cower before You. (66:3).
All the earth bows down to You; they sing praise to You; they sing praise to Your name.” Selah (66:4).
Come and see the works of God; how awesome are His deeds toward mankind. (66:5).
He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him. (66:6).
He rules forever by His power; His eyes watch the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah (66:7).
Bless our God, O peoples; let the sound of His praise be heard. (66:8).
He preserves our lives and keeps our feet from slipping. (66:9).
For You , O God, have tested us; You have refined us like silver. (66:10).
You led us into the net; You laid burdens on our backs. (66:11).
You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water, but You brought us into abundance. (66:12).
I will enter Your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to You — (66:13).
the vows that my lips promised and my mouth spoke in my distress. (66:14).
I will offer You fatlings as burnt offerings, with the fragrant smoke of rams; I will offer bulls and goats. Selah (66:15).
Come and listen, all you who fear God, and I will declare what He has done for me. (66:16).
I cried out to Him with my mouth and praised Him with my tongue. (66:17).
If I had cherished iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not have listened. (66:18).
But God has surely heard; He has attended to the sound of my prayer. (66:19).
Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer or withheld from me His loving devotion! (66:20).
crossRefs: Exodus 14:21–22: Sea turned to dry land.
Joshua 3:14–17: Crossing the Jordan on dry ground.
Malachi 3:3: Refining like silver.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צָרַף (tsaraf), Greek: δοκιμάζω/χωνεύω, Aramaic: צרף
Hebrew: רְוָיָה (revayah), Greek: πλησμονή, Aramaic: רוויה

stories.keyTakeaway: All peoples are called to see God’s deeds, as the psalm recounts deliverance through testing and affirms answered prayer.

stories.title: 🌍 Psalms 67
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song. May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah (67:1).
that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations. (67:2).
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You. (67:3).
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah (67:4).
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You. (67:5).
The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us. (67:6).
God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him. (67:7).
crossRefs: Numbers 6:24–26: Priestly blessing with shining face.
Genesis 12:3: Blessing to all families of the earth.
Revelation 7:9–10: All nations crying out in salvation.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָאֵר פָּנָיו (yaʾer panav), Greek: φωτίσαι τὸ πρόσωπον, Aramaic: נהיר אפוהי
Hebrew: מֵישָׁרִים (meysharim), Greek: εὐθύτης, Aramaic: מישרין

stories.keyTakeaway: A prayer for God’s blessing so that all nations know, rejoice, and praise Him as the earth yields its harvest.

headings.text: May God Cause His Face to Shine upon Us

stories.title: 🛡️ Psalms 68
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. A song. God arises. His enemies are scattered, and those who hate Him flee His presence. (68:1).
As smoke is blown away, You will drive them out; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked will perish in the presence of God. (68:2).
But the righteous will be glad and rejoice before God; they will celebrate with joy. (68:3).
Sing to God! Sing praises to His name. Exalt Him who rides on the clouds— His name is the LORD— and rejoice before Him. (68:4).
A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in His holy habitation. (68:5).
God settles the lonely in families; He leads the prisoners out to prosperity, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land. (68:6).
O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wasteland, Selah (68:7).
the earth shook and the heavens poured down rain before God, the One on Sinai, before God, the God of Israel. (68:8).
You sent abundant rain, O God; You refreshed Your weary inheritance. (68:9).
Your flock settled therein; O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor. (68:10).
The Lord gives the command; a great company of women proclaim it: (68:11).
“Kings and their armies flee in haste; she who waits at home divides the plunder. (68:12).
Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold.” (68:13).
When the Almighty scattered the kings in the land, it was like the snow falling on Zalmon. (68:14).
A mountain of God is Mount Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is Mount Bashan. (68:15).
Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever. (68:16).
The chariots of God are tens of thousands — thousands of thousands are they; the Lord is in His sanctuary as He was at Sinai. (68:17).
You have ascended on high; You have led captives away. You have received gifts from men, even from the rebellious, that the LORD God may dwell there. (68:18).
Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah (68:19).
Our God is a God of deliverance; the Lord GOD is our rescuer from death. (68:20).
Surely God will crush the heads of His enemies, the hairy crowns of those who persist in guilty ways. (68:21).
The Lord said, “I will retrieve them from Bashan, I will bring them up from the depths of the sea, (68:22).
that your foot may be dipped in the blood of your foes— the tongues of your dogs in the same.” (68:23).
They have seen Your procession, O God — the march of my God and King into the sanctuary. (68:24).
The singers lead the way, the musicians follow after, among the maidens playing tambourines. (68:25).
Bless God in the great congregation; bless the LORD from the fountain of Israel. (68:26).
There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah in their company, the princes of Zebulun and of Naphtali. (68:27).
Summon Your power, O God; show Your strength, O God, which You have exerted on our behalf. (68:28).
Because of Your temple at Jerusalem kings will bring You gifts. (68:29).
Rebuke the beast in the reeds, the herd of bulls among the calves of the nations, until it submits, bringing bars of silver. Scatter the nations who delight in war. (68:30).
Envoys will arrive from Egypt; Cush will stretch out her hands to God. (68:31).
Sing to God, O kingdoms of the earth; sing praises to the Lord— Selah (68:32).
to Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old; behold, His mighty voice resounds. (68:33).
Ascribe the power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, whose strength is in the skies. (68:34).
O God, You are awesome in Your sanctuary; the God of Israel Himself gives strength and power to His people. Blessed be God! (68:35).
crossRefs: Numbers 10:35: “Let God arise” as Israel sets out.
Ephesians 4:8: Cites “You ascended on high… and received gifts.”
Deuteronomy 33:2–5: The LORD coming from Sinai to rule.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (ʿalita la-marom), Greek (LXX): ἀνέβης εἰς ὕψος, Aramaic: סליקת למרום
translationNotes.note: Victory ascent with captives and gifts (v. 18).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲבִי יְתוֹמִים (ʾavi yetomim), Greek: πατὴρ ὀρφανῶν, Aramaic: אבא דיתומין

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm recounts God’s victorious march and care for the vulnerable, His enthronement in Zion, and a call for all kingdoms to praise Him.

stories.title: 🌊 Psalms 69
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “Lilies.” Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck. (69:1).
I have sunk into the miry depths, where there is no footing; I have drifted into deep waters, where the flood engulfs me. (69:2).
I am weary from my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes fail, looking for my God. (69:3).
Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head; many are those who would destroy me — my enemies for no reason. Though I did not steal, I must repay. (69:4).
You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You. (69:5).
May those who hope in You not be ashamed through me, O Lord GOD of Hosts; may those who seek You not be dishonored through me, O God of Israel. (69:6).
For I have endured scorn for Your sake, and shame has covered my face. (69:7).
I have become a stranger to my brothers and a foreigner to my mother’s sons, (69:8).
because zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me. (69:9).
I wept and fasted, but it brought me reproach. (69:10).
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I was sport to them. (69:11).
Those who sit at the gate mock me, and I am the song of drunkards. (69:12).
But my prayer to You, O LORD, is for a time of favor. In Your abundant loving devotion, O God, answer me with Your sure salvation. (69:13).
Rescue me from the mire and do not let me sink; deliver me from my foes and out of the deep waters. (69:14).
Do not let the floods engulf me or the depths swallow me up; let not the Pit close its mouth over me. (69:15).
Answer me, O LORD, for Your loving devotion is good; turn to me in keeping with Your great compassion. (69:16).
Hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in distress. Answer me quickly! (69:17).
Draw near to my soul and redeem me; ransom me because of my foes. (69:18).
You know my reproach, my shame and disgrace. All my adversaries are before You. (69:19).
Insults have broken my heart, and I am in despair. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, for comforters, but I found no one. (69:20).
They poisoned my food with gall and gave me vinegar to quench my thirst. (69:21).
May their table become a snare; may it be a retribution and a trap. (69:22).
May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever. (69:23).
Pour out Your wrath upon them, and let Your burning anger overtake them. (69:24).
May their place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in their tents. (69:25).
For they persecute the one You struck and recount the pain of those You wounded. (69:26).
Add iniquity to their iniquity; let them not share in Your righteousness. (69:27).
May they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous. (69:28).
But I am in pain and distress; let Your salvation protect me, O God. (69:29).
I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving. (69:30).
And this will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves. (69:31).
The humble will see and rejoice. You who seek God, let your hearts be revived! (69:32).
For the LORD listens to the needy and does not despise His captive people. (69:33).
Let heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moves in them. (69:34).
For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and possess it. (69:35).
The descendants of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will settle in it. (69:36).
crossRefs: John 2:17: “Zeal for Your house” applied to Jesus.
John 19:28–29: Gall and vinegar given.
Acts 1:20; Romans 11:9–10: Quotations of the imprecations.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֹאשׁ (rosh, ‘gall/poison’) / חֹמֶץ (chometz, ‘vinegar’), Greek: χολή / ὄξος, Aramaic: ראשא / חמאץ
Hebrew: חֶרְפָּה (ḥerpah), Greek: ὀνειδισμός, Aramaic: חרפתא

translationNotes.note: A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂק (saq); Greek: σάκκος (sakkos)

translationNotes.note: Far more than an entrance; the public square where elders heard legal cases, contracts were witnessed, market business transacted, and news was exchanged. 'Sitting in the gate' (Genesis 19:1; Ruth 4:1-11; Proverbs 31:23) signals civic authority and active community life.
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁעַר (sha'ar)

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm portrays overwhelming reproach and unjust suffering, petitions for judgment on enemies, and closes with praise and hope for Zion.

headings.text: The Waters Are up to My Neck

stories.title: ⏩ Psalms 70
summaryBullets: For the choirmaster. Of David. To bring remembrance. Make haste, O God, to deliver me! Hurry, O LORD, to help me! (70:1).
May those who seek my life be ashamed and confounded; may those who wish me harm be repelled and humiliated. (70:2).
May those who say, “Aha, aha!” retreat because of their shame. (70:3).
May all who seek You rejoice and be glad in You; may those who love Your salvation always say, “Let God be magnified!” (70:4).
But I am poor and needy; hurry to me, O God. You are my help and my deliverer; O LORD, do not delay. (70:5).
crossRefs: Psalm 40:13–17: Parallel lines reused.
Psalm 35:4: Let those who seek my life be put to shame.
Philippians 4:4: Rejoice in the Lord (response theme).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חוּשָׁה (chushah), Greek: σπεῦσον, Aramaic: חוּש
Hebrew: עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן (ʿani ve-ʾevyon), Greek: πτωχὸς καὶ πένης, Aramaic: מסכן ועביוֹן

stories.keyTakeaway: A brief urgent plea for swift deliverance and for the shame of enemies, with a call for seekers of God to rejoice.

headings.text: Hurry, O Lord, to Help Me!

stories.title: 🧓 Psalms 71
summaryBullets: In You, O LORD, I have taken refuge; let me never be put to shame. (71:1).
In Your justice, rescue and deliver me; incline Your ear and save me. (71:2).
Be my rock of refuge, where I can always go. Give the command to save me, for You are my rock and my fortress. (71:3).
Deliver me, O my God, from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and ruthless. (71:4).
For You are my hope, O Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth. (71:5).
I have leaned on You since birth; You pulled me from my mother’s womb. My praise is always for You. (71:6).
I have become a portent to many, but You are my strong refuge. (71:7).
My mouth is filled with Your praise and with Your splendor all day long. (71:8).
Do not discard me in my old age; do not forsake me when my strength fails. (71:9).
For my enemies speak against me, and those who lie in wait for my life conspire, (71:10).
saying, “God has forsaken him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.” (71:11).
Be not far from me, O God. Hurry, O my God, to help me. (71:12).
May the accusers of my soul be ashamed and consumed; may those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace. (71:13).
But I will always hope and will praise You more and more. (71:14).
My mouth will declare Your righteousness and Your salvation all day long, though I cannot know their full measure. (71:15).
I will come in the strength of the Lord GOD; I will proclaim Your righteousness — Yours alone. (71:16).
O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds. (71:17).
Even when I am old and gray, do not forsake me, O God, until I proclaim Your power to the next generation, Your might to all who are to come. (71:18).
Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, O God, You who have done great things. Who, O God, is like You? (71:19).
Though You have shown me many troubles and misfortunes, You will revive me once again. Even from the depths of the earth You will bring me back up. (71:20).
You will increase my honor and comfort me once again. (71:21).
So I will praise You with the harp for Your faithfulness, O my God; I will sing praise to You with the lyre, O Holy One of Israel. (71:22).
When I sing praise to You my lips will shout for joy, along with my soul, which You have redeemed. (71:23).
My tongue will indeed proclaim Your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm are disgraced and confounded. (71:24).
crossRefs: Isaiah 46:4: “Even to your old age I am He… I will carry.”
Psalm 22:9–10: Trust from birth.
2 Samuel 22:2–3: The LORD as rock, fortress, and deliverer.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קְדוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (qedosh Yisraʾel), Greek: ὁ ἅγιος Ἰσραήλ, Aramaic: קדישא דישראל
translationNotes.note: Title for God used in praise (v. 22).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֵׂיבָה (seivah), Greek: πολιὰ, Aramaic: סֵיבַתָּא
translationNotes.note: Old age marker in the plea for continued help (v. 18).

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm asks God to sustain and deliver in old age and vows continual praise from youth to gray hairs.

stories.title: 👑 Psalms 72
summaryBullets: Of Solomon. Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness. (72:1).
May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice. (72:2).
May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness. (72:3).
May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor. (72:4).
May they fear him as long as the sun shines, as long as the moon remains, through all generations. (72:5).
May he be like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth. (72:6).
May the righteous flourish in his days and prosperity abound until the moon is no more. (72:7).
May he rule from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth. (72:8).
May the nomads bow before him, and his enemies lick the dust. (72:9).
May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts. (72:10).
May all kings bow down to him and all nations serve him. (72:11).
For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper. (72:12).
He will take pity on the poor and needy and save the lives of the oppressed. (72:13).
He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight. (72:14).
Long may he live! May gold from Sheba be given him. May people ever pray for him; may they bless him all day long. (72:15).
May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills. May its fruit trees flourish like the forests of Lebanon, the people of its cities like the grass of the field. (72:16).
May his name endure forever; may his name continue as long as the sun shines. In him may all nations be blessed; may they call him blessed. (72:17).
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds. (72:18).
And blessed be His glorious name forever; may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen. (72:19).
Thus conclude the prayers of David son of Jesse. (72:20).
crossRefs: Zechariah 9:10: Rule “from sea to sea.”
1 Kings 10:1–10: Gifts from the queen of Sheba.
Genesis 22:18: All nations blessed in Abraham’s offspring.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִיָּם עַד־יָם (mi-yam ʿad-yam), Greek: ἀπὸ θαλάσσης ἕως θαλάσσης, Aramaic: מן ימא ועד ימא
Hebrew: שְׁבָא (Sheva), Greek: Σαβά, Aramaic: שבא
translationNotes.note: Southern Arabian kingdom named among gift-bringers (v. 10).

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm petitions for a just, worldwide-reigning king who defends the poor and brings flourishing, concluding with a doxology.

headings.text: Endow the King with Your Justice

stories.title: 👀 Psalms 73
summaryBullets: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart. (73:1).
But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped. (73:2).
For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked. (73:3).
They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed. (73:4).
They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men. (73:5).
Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them. (73:6).
From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild. (73:7).
They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression. (73:8).
They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth. (73:9).
So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance. (73:10).
The wicked say, “How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?” (73:11).
Behold, these are the wicked — always carefree as they increase their wealth. (73:12).
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands. (73:13).
For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning. (73:14).
If I had said, “I will speak this way,” then I would have betrayed Your children. (73:15).
When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight (73:16).
until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end. (73:17).
Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin. (73:18).
How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors! (73:19).
Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form. (73:20).
When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within, (73:21).
I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You. (73:22).
Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand. (73:23).
You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory. (73:24).
Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You. (73:25).
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever. (73:26).
Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You. (73:27).
But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works. (73:28).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 12:1–2: Questioning the prosperity of the wicked.
Psalm 16:5: The LORD is my portion.
Psalm 37: Do not fret because of evildoers.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִקְדָּשׁ (mikdash), Greek: ἅγιον, Aramaic: מקדשא
translationNotes.note: Holy place where understanding is gained (v. 17).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֵלֶק (cheleq), Greek: μερὶς, Aramaic: מְנָתָא
translationNotes.note: Share/inheritance; used for the LORD as one’s lasting share (v. 26).

stories.keyTakeaway: The psalm moves from envy at the ease of the wicked to recognition of their end and declares God as lasting portion and refuge.

headings.text: BOOK III Surely God Is Good to Israel

stories.title: 🏚️ Psalms 74
summaryBullets: A Maskil of Asaph. Why have You rejected us forever, O God? Why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture? (74:1).
Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance — Mount Zion, where You dwell. (74:2).
Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed. (74:3).
Your foes have roared within Your meeting place; they have unfurled their banners as signs, (74:4).
like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees (74:5).
and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks. (74:6).
They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground; they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name. (74:7).
They said in their hearts, “We will crush them completely.” They burned down every place where God met us in the land. (74:8).
There are no signs for us to see. There is no longer any prophet. And none of us knows how long this will last. (74:9).
How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You? Will the foe revile Your name forever? (74:10).
Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand? Stretch it out to destroy them! (74:11).
Yet God is my King from ancient times, working salvation on the earth. (74:12).
You divided the sea by Your strength; You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea; (74:13).
You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You fed him to the creatures of the desert. (74:14).
You broke open the fountain and the flood; You dried up the ever-flowing rivers. (74:15).
The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun. (74:16).
You set all the boundaries of the earth; You made the summer and winter. (74:17).
Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD, how a foolish people has spurned Your name. (74:18).
Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts; do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever. (74:19).
Consider Your covenant, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land. (74:20).
